result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow, partially obstructed sidewalks and a lack of marked crossings at the visible intersection. Parked vehicles on both sides of the street create significant visual obstructions, reducing safety for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb line obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross in unmarked areas.

hazards.name: Narrow sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is narrow and partially obstructed by building features.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalk markings at the intersection to define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past parked cars.

interventions.title: Sidewalk widening
interventions.description: Widen the existing sidewalks to provide a clear, unobstructed path of travel.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow residential street with row houses and a continuous paved sidewalk. While the environment is low-speed, pedestrian safety is compromised by utility pole obstructions and visual barriers created by parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: A wooden utility pole is located directly in the middle of the sidewalk path, narrowing the effective width for pedestrians and mobility devices.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, on the sidewalk in front of the brick row house.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Large parked vehicles, including a pickup truck, block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and right side along the curb line.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near intersections or mid-block crossing points to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Implement a furniture or planting zone between the sidewalk and the curb to house utility poles and provide physical separation from traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street with continuous sidewalks and parallel parking on both sides. While the narrow roadway geometry likely encourages lower vehicle speeds, there is a lack of physical buffers or traffic calming measures to enhance pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street limits sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who may step into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Calming
hazards.description: The absence of physical speed control measures on a residential street may lead to unsafe vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install speed humps or speed cushions to physically enforce low speeds in this residential environment.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at the nearest intersections to improve visibility and reduce the crossing distance for pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential sidewalk that is significantly obstructed by a large metal staircase enclosure and trash storage area. Parked vehicles directly adjacent to the curb create a visual barrier between the walkway and the roadway, and there is no buffer zone for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large metal cage enclosing a staircase and trash bins significantly reduces the effective width of the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into a narrow path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, attached to the brick building and extending onto the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, left and right sides along the curb.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearance
interventions.description: Relocate or redesign the staircase enclosure and trash storage to restore the full width of the pedestrian walkway.
